- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates subsequent decline or stabilization.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values, particularly in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate price pullback after sharp rises.
- Overshoot after spikes is common: model forecasts peak immediately after a spike, then fails to adjust downward.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days shows significant lag; model reacts too slowly to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates late-period price increases (especially 28–30 days) — often misses upward momentum.
- Model overfits recent trends, leading to overconfidence in short-term continuation.
- Price corrections after spikes are not adequately modeled — model fails to capture “rebound” or “reversion” phases.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — once a price level is exceeded, it tends to stay above or below, ignoring volatility.
